title: Load test of the shared stack, including the index-backed home page and one noisy tenant
description:
Outcome: Before TI moves: 50 synthetic tenants on staging, each with stories and References; readers hitting home, section and story pages through the edge; editors publishing; monitors delivering 30 References a run; one tenant doing a full re-render. Measure: p95 publish-to-live, AppSync requests per change (must stay proportional to the change; PPY-3fd0aa), Lambda concurrency, queue wait per tenant, edge hit ratio, cost per tenant per day. The home page must use the index-backed blocks (PPY-7f1e54), not the whole-corpus snapshot (PPY-ee02b8).

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): a load script (k6 or Python) under scripts/load/, staging shared stack, request meter, CloudWatch dashboards.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/shared-stack-load.feature):
Scenario: One noisy tenant does not slow the others
    Given 50 tenants and one running a full re-render
    When the other tenants publish
    Then their p95 publish-to-live stays within the agreed bound and AppSync calls per change do not grow with tenant count

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-3bbbf9, PPY-994bd0, PPY-413576, PPY-7f1e54. Blocks PPY-04ce84. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: -.

Testing: It is the test; results on this issue.
Rollout: Staging.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: the load test costs money. Mitigation: a bounded run with a stated budget, approved beforehand.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: unchanged.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
